name: Darius
notes: Noxian Guillotine's real cast is deliberately delayed past the automatic t=0 opening: it fires the first time Hemorrhage reaches its 5-stack cap (usually within a couple of seconds of autos/Q/W), so its true-damage multiplier is at the full +100% for the one cast that fits in a short fight; the engine still primes Spellblade and delays the first attack by 0.25s at t=0 regardless.

Decimate is assumed to land with the outer 'blade' radius on the dummy (full damage, applies a Hemorrhage stack), never the reduced 35% 'handle' damage, since a well-played Darius would position to hit with the blade.

Decimate's 0.75s wind-up (its 'cast time' is stated as none on the wiki) blocks basic attacks for that duration but is not treated as the engine's 0.25s ABILITY_LOCKOUT_S cast-time delay; its cooldown starts when the swing lands (post-effect).

Crippling Strike is woven in right after an attack lands (mirroring an Empower-style attack reset): it arms the next attack, which lands one windup later and resets the attack timer; its cooldown starts when that attack lands (post-effect). We used the wiki's plain-text 40-60% bonus AD reading rather than the sheet's ADRatio (1.4-1.6) column, since that column's own tooltip note shows it already includes the attack's own 100% AD, i.e. bonus = ADRatio - 1.0 matches the wiki's 40-60%.

Apprehend (E) is never cast: its active pull/slow deals no damage against an already-in-range stationary target, and its passive percent armor penetration modifies the caster's own mitigation math in a way this engine's damage pipeline (target debuffs only) has no hook for, so it is omitted entirely.

Hemorrhage's bleed uses the wiki's stated 1.25s tick interval (over the bin's 1.26s) and is modeled as a single DoT per target whose per-tick damage scales with Darius' current stack count on the target; every damaging attack or ability refreshes the stack count (capped at 5) and the 5s duration, consistent with 'refreshing on subsequent applications'.

Bleed ticks are treated as passive damage, not ability-cast damage, given the dossier's own unresolved note about Hemorrhage's spell-effect/proc tagging; this means they do not trigger ability-damage-keyed item effects.

Noxian Might (the bonus AD buff) is modeled as edge-triggered: it fires the moment stacks climb from below 5 up to the 5-stack cap, and will not refire while stacks are simply held at the cap, matching 'applies maximum stacks' as a one-time event rather than a sustained condition.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds inside a short fight at level 16.
